report:
The evidence does not support the claim that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19.

**Origin of the claim:** In March 2020, French Health Minister Olivier Véran tweeted a warning against NSAIDs for COVID-19 symptoms, based on a Lancet hypothesis that anti-inflammatories might upregulate ACE2 receptors (the SARS-CoV-2 entry point), theoretically worsening infection ([sciencealert.com](https://www.sciencealert.com/who-recommends-to-avoid-taking-ibuprofen-for-covid-19-symptoms)). This sparked global alarm and a temporary WHO caution, but WHO quickly reversed course, stating there was no evidence ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 outcomes ([cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ibuprofen-covid-19-novel-coronavirus-1.5501496)).

**Subsequent research:** A systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies (covering positivity risk, hospitalization, death, and severe composite outcomes) found no consistent evidence that NSAID/ibuprofen use increases COVID-19 severity or mortality ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8327046](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8327046/)). A 38-day cohort study similarly found no significant association between NSAID use and worse clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579/)). Additional studies, including one in Infectious Diseases and Therapy, concluded ibuprofen/NSAID use was "not associated" with worse outcomes ([link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40121-020-00363-w](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40121-020-00363-w)).

**Conclusion:** The claim originated from a plausible but unproven biological hypothesis and a single official's precautionary tweet—not from solid clinical data. Larger reviews and cohort studies conducted since 2020 have not confirmed it. Major health authorities (WHO, NHS, EMA) ultimately concluded ibuprofen can be used safely for COVID-19 symptoms, though some clinicians still prefer acetaminophen as a first-line choice out of caution. Overall, the claim that ibuprofen "worsens" COVID-19 infection is not well supported by current evidence.
